{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABf_Fg1Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhJcOIs", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 398, "title": "Simplify Graph Editor variable-input controls: remove redundant counts and explanatory prose", "body": "## Problem

Graph Editor's right-hand **Settings** Inspector shows redundant variable-input UI instead of communicating the operation through layout. The current `GraphEditor.drawInspector()` in `extension/graph-editor.js`:

- For `TextProcessingLfm2` and `TextProcessingQwen35`, renders an editable **`Input count (1–32)` number field** even though users can already add/remove inputs.
- For **Text Processing, Display, and TextFormatter**, always renders a paragraph starting with `N TEXT/ITEM inputs.` and explaining behaviors such as **"Removed inputs keep their wires as visible validation errors; disconnect them explicitly."**, **"Remove deletes only the last input and its wire."**, plus tab/prompt/template/session explanations.
- Places **Add input / Remove last input** among this permanent prose, making an otherwise simple operation harder to scan.

The numeric count is an internal persisted setting, not useful additional UI information: the numbered input ports already appear on the graph canvas. This conflicts with the established [UI/UX principles](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/README.md#uiux): **Keep it simple**, **Show, don't tell**, and **Intuitive and predictable**. As explicitly stated there, this must **not** remove essential control labels, accessible names, errors, or information necessary to operate the interface.

This is a **presentation/interaction cleanup**, not a request to change input-port contracts or edge-removal semantics. Related precedent: #148 (UI principles), #304 (remove redundant Inspector help), #389 (Text Processing input behavior), and #216 (Display tab semantics).

## Expected outcome

### 1. Compact, consistent variable-input controls

In Graph Editor → Settings for **`TextProcessingLfm2`, `TextProcessingQwen35`, `Display`, and `TextFormatter`**:

- Present a compact, clearly grouped **Inputs** section with adjacent **add (+)** and **remove-last (−)** actions. Grouping, proximity, spacing and affordance—not a paragraph—must communicate that the actions change the node's input ports. Follow the existing Inspector visual language rather than introducing a new component system.
- **Remove the visible editable `Input count (1–32)` field** from both Text Processing variants. Do **not** replace it with a read-only numeric count, counter badge, `N inputs` label, or separate instruction.
- **Remove the always-visible explanatory `N TEXT/ITEM inputs. …` paragraph** from all four node types. Do not recreate this prose elsewhere as a replacement help block or a new permanent tooltip.
- Keep meaningful labels that are truly needed: **Inputs**, **System prompt**, and the existing editable **Display input tab labels** (including their distinguishable `Input N` identity/fallback). Arrange Display's tab-label controls coherently with the input section without losing editability.
- Each action must have an **accessible name** (e.g. `Add input`, `Remove last input`), an obvious keyboard focus indication, and native button/keyboard semantics. A visual icon alone must not remove assistive-technology meaning. Use appropriately sized/clickable controls on narrow screens; do not introduce inaccessible icon-only buttons.
- Retain visible **contextual validation/error feedback and recovery actions** when there really is a problem. "Show, don't tell" applies to *permanent redundant explanation*, not actionable errors.

### 2. Preserve all existing behavior

- **Do not remove or rename `settings.inputCount`** in any node or JSON representation, nor change defaults/allowed bounds, port names/types/order (`input1…inputN`), the System prompt, Display tab labels, TextFormatter template semantics, or runtime/model behavior.
- Preserve existing incremental add / remove-last behavior and disabled boundary states (Text Processing and Display: **1–32**; TextFormatter: its existing supported bounds/validation). Count changes must immediately update visible canvas ports and remain compatible with Auto Save, Undo/Redo, JSON import/export, and reload.
- Crucial intentional difference when *removing a connected input*: **Text Processing retains the obsolete wire**, producing its current visible unknown-port validation error and an explicit **Disconnect** recovery action; an invalid draft must not silently overwrite a valid saved graph or reroute the edge. **Display and TextFormatter retain their existing remove-last-wire behavior**. This distinction must stay functional without explaining it permanently in the Inspector.
- Preserve Display's remaining tab labels and connections, the single-input/tab behavior, and the existing graph selection/focus/connection-inspection behavior. Existing accessible canvas port names and types must remain available.
- Keep this limited to the Graph Editor Settings presentation and the directly affected UI tests/documentation. No graph-schema migration, model-weight download, unrelated Help/Library/Live redesign, or speculative framework.

### Pre-merge acceptance criteria (automatable)

- [ ] For both Text Processing models, selecting the node shows the compact Inputs controls, **no visible or editable `Input count` field**, and no permanent `N TEXT inputs` / removed-wire explanation. The System prompt remains editable.
- [ ] For Display and TextFormatter, the same compact, consistent add/remove arrangement appears **without** permanent `N ITEM/TEXT inputs` or behavior-help paragraphs. Display's title/tab labels and TextFormatter's template are unchanged and usable.
- [ ] Actions change the expected numbered canvas ports; minimum/maximum limits and disabled states work; keyboard activation, accessible names and focus states work. Check narrow **320/390 px** and desktop editor layouts without Inspector overflow or overlapping controls.
- [ ] Both Text Processing variants pass a connected-input removal regression: obsolete edge remains, a real validation error and explicit Disconnect are available, no silent rewire/persistence of the invalid draft; resolving or undoing the edit restores valid behavior.
- [ ] Display/TextFormatter keep their original last-port/last-wire deletion behavior; remaining Display input tab labels and edge identities are preserved.
- [ ] Auto Save, Undo/Redo, export/import and reload preserve `settings.inputCount` and other settings after +/- edits, including boundary conditions. Existing graph data and model/inference behavior have not changed.
- [ ] Update the affected UI assertions that currently *depend on the numeric field*, including `tests/extension/graph-text-summary.spec.js` (presently uses `getByLabel('… Input count')`, `fill('32')`, `fill('2')`). Add focused negative assertions for removed persistent copy and positive checks for actions/validation/accessibility. Use existing Display/TextFormatter/editor test fixtures and avoid duplicating broad integration coverage.
- [ ] Run applicable fast tests and UI coverage following [development-flow test/CI principles](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md#test-and-ci-principles): `npm test`, focused Chromium/WebKit browser Graph Editor checks, focused MV3 Graph Editor / Text Processing / Display tests, and affected regression suites where feasible. Clearly report anything skipped or environment-blocked; no real AI-model download is needed solely to check this Inspector UI.
- [ ] Update only genuinely affected user-facing instructions (e.g. `docs/text-summary-nodes.md` where it says "Set Input count to 2", plus applicable Graph Editor UI instructions) to say **add/remove inputs**, while retaining accurate technical documentation of persisted `inputCount` and the distinct port/edge semantics. Verify documentation links and `git diff --check`.

## Required post-merge verification

**None.** This Inspector change can be validated before merge with source, automated tests and browser/extension UI checks. Do not introduce a deployment or human-approval gate without a concrete need.

## Context

**Relevant code:**
- [`extension/graph-editor.js` — `drawInspector()` and `resizeInputs()`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph-editor.js): current number input, persistent paragraph, add/remove buttons, obsolete-wire recovery, and type-specific deletion behavior.
- [`extension/graph.css`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph.css): Inspector layout and responsive styling.
- [`extension/graph.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/extension/graph.js), [`web/display-node.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/web/display-node.js), [`docs/text-summary-nodes.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/text-summary-nodes.md), [`docs/extension-graph.md`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/extension-graph.md): preserved schema, bounds, graph and Display semantics.
- [`tests/extension/graph-text-summary.spec.js`](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/tests/extension/graph-text-summary.spec.js): existing count-field and removed-wire regression coverage; update when removing that field.
- [Issue template](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/issue.md), [development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md), and [review guidelines](https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md). Follow Issue → implementation → PR → review → merge, with English collaboration artifacts.

**How to observe the problem:** Open Graph Editor, select either Text Processing model, and inspect the Settings sidebar; `Input count (1–32)` appears above the long `N TEXT inputs…` paragraph and Add/Remove buttons. Select Display or TextFormatter to see the same redundant descriptive paragraph. After this issue, +/- and visible ports should tell the story; actual validation errors must still explain recovery only when needed.
